title: Two Shadows? Vector Components Explained Simply | PUC Physics Class 11
description:
A kite string pulls up and sideways. A ball flies forward and up. Aarav rides 10 m up a slope. Each moves in one direction, but we usually want two answers: how far forward, and how high? In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Physics (NCERT Chapter 3, Motion in a Plane) we learn to resolve a vector into its components.

We split one arrow into its x and y shadows, turn it in a live simulation while the components trace cosine and sine curves, and see a component turn negative past 90°. Then we derive Ax = A cos θ and Ay = A sin θ from one right triangle, get the size back with Pythagoras and the direction with tan θ = Ay/Ax. Two pause-and-think questions, a worked example on Aarav's slope, the exam trap about where θ is measured, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, JEE Main and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 A kite, a ball and a bicycle: one arrow, two questions
0:25 What does it mean to resolve a vector?
0:58 The turning arrow: components on a live graph
1:39 Why cos and sin, step by step
2:28 Side by side + pause and think
3:23 Worked example: Aarav on a 30° slope
4:03 Exam trap: where is θ measured?
4:25 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
4:58 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Unit Vectors. What if every vector could be built from tiny arrows of length one?
